factory_wide_operational_requirements: AUDIT ARTIFACT PLACEMENT (applies to every core-lane and Frontier independent audit). The gate reader runs `jq -e '.gate=="PASS" or .gate=="REVISE" or .gate=="BLOCKED"' results/audit/<lane>/CYCLE_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_GATE.json` against the AUDIT JOB CHECKOUT, i.e. the repository root you are currently in. Write results/audit/<lane>/CYCLE_<run_id>_GATE.json and reports/audit/<lane>/CYCLE_<run_id>.md there, using exactly those relative paths from your current working directory. Do NOT write them into /tmp/lex_team (the producer worktree): artifacts left there are invisible to the gate reader, the audit job fails with `jq: error: Could not open file ...`, no promotion happens and the lane re-dispatches forever. Verified this cycle: runs 38571087814 and 38578725589 failed this way; run 38559540834 passed when the same auditor used relative paths. This is a file-location contract only — the gate verdict stays fully independent.

DIRECTOR BASE-SHA GUARD MISFIRES ON REPAIR RUNS (control-plane hardening item; .github/** is control-plane scope and is NOT edited from here). factory-director.yml records reports/director/BASE_DIRECTION_SHA_<run>.txt at the 'Record control-plane base' step AFTER 'Restore exact rejected proposal for repair', so on a repair run the recorded base is the REJECTED PROPOSAL's direction sha rather than main's. Verified in run 38786736419: the workflow-recorded value was 02351c26... (rejected proposal v52) while origin/main:state/factory_direction.json is 52f704ed... (v51, unchanged since run 38784614826 recorded exactly that value). On a PASS the integrate job compares the recorded base with main's current sha and would therefore skip integration with a spurious 'Superseded Director proposal' warning for EVERY repair round. Intended fix (owner/control-plane maintainer): record the base before restoring the rejected proposal, or inherit origin/<rejected-run>/reports/director/BASE_DIRECTION_SHA_<rejected-run>.txt on repair runs. Route-around used this round: the repair republished the TRUE control-plane base (52f704ed...) in its own BASE file and discloses both values in reports/director/RUN_38786736419.md; the supersession check still works as designed because main had not moved.

THE SUPERVISOR'S 'EXHAUSTED SAME-CHARTER WORK' GUARD IS DEAD CODE, BECAUSE jq's // OPERATOR TREATS LITERAL false AS EMPTY. Read at .github/workflows/factory-supervisor.yml:277 and reproduced locally with jq 1.7 this run: the guard evaluates `jq -r '.continue_recommended // true' <<<"$raw"` and compares the result to the string false, but `echo '{"continue_recommended":false}' | jq -r '.continue_recommended // true'` prints `true`, because jq's alternative operator falls through on false as well as on null. The guard can therefore NEVER fire, and any team whose lab/frontier/<team>.json says continue_recommended:false is re-dispatched forever. Observed live: frontier-counter-label-integrity was dispatched at 06:35Z (run 38862093221, cancelled) and again at 07:47Z (run 38869446783) while its accepted branch state already read charter_version 1, cycle_status TERMINATE, continue_recommended false -- producing at least nine no-change verification cycles and eight producer-authored audit placement copies. The identical pattern is on line 230 for the CORE lanes' .continue_recommended check, so a core lane can also be re-dispatched after it declares itself exhausted. .github/** is control-plane scope and is NOT edited from a lane, a team or the director. ROUTE-AROUND, and this is the standing rule rather than a one-off fix: the portfolio .status field is the ONLY reliable stop, because the dispatch query at line 261 is `select(.status=="RUN")`, a plain string comparison the jq defect does not touch. Set a discharged or exhausted team's status to TERMINATED; do not rely on continue_recommended, do not rely on a blocker file, and do not re-dispatch it. Intended upstream fix for the control-plane maintainer: test the field with `jq -r 'if .continue_recommended == false then "false" else "true" end'` (or `.continue_recommended | tostring`), never with //.

AUDIT GATE FILENAME IS CASE-SENSITIVE AND THE AUDITOR PLAN TEXT OFTEN GETS IT WRONG. Observed this run on core product run 38897640010: the GitHub REST job record establishes that the audit job FAILED at the step 'Enforce audit scope and read gate' and that integrate was skipped, but the job logs return HTTP 403 unauthenticated, so the lowercase-filename attribution is an INFERENCE, not established fact (that step also contains the write-scope check, the other possible cause) and it must be hedged as 'almost certainly' until a log line is read. The inference rests on the auditor plan text for that run having printed 'Write reports/audit/product/CYCLE_38897640010.md and results/audit/product/CYCLE_38897640010_gate.json' (lowercase _gate). The workflow reader runs jq on results/audit/product/CYCLE_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_GATE.json. A lowercase file is invisible to the reader, the audit job fails with jq: error / exit 2, no promotion happens, and the lane re-dispatches. This is the same placement class as writing into /tmp/lex_team, one character different. Standing rule for every core-lane and Frontier auditor: the gate path is results/audit/<lane>/CYCLE_<run_id>_GATE.json with UPPERCASE _GATE.json; write exactly that relative path from the audit-job checkout; never /tmp/lex_team; never a lowercase suffix. .github/** is control-plane scope and is NOT edited from a lane or from the director; the requirement is restated here so the next auditor prompt-consuming agent sees it.

SET-IDENTITY CLAIMS ABOUT ACCEPTED EVIDENCE MUST BE VERIFIED AS SET RELATIONS, NEVER BY MATCHING CARDINALITIES. Verified this repair round (audit A-1 against director run 38906250297): reports/director/RUN_38906250297.md section 3 asserted, inside the table it heads 'every number recomputed this run from the accepted mount', that 'the 16 absent rows are exactly the 16 UNBACKED, supported=false rows'. Independent recomputation over the accepted artifact results/frontier/frontier-served-packet-falsification/LABEL_HALF.json bundles[*].rows (n=65 = 25 de + 15 fr + 25 it) on (primary_defect_class, counter_evidence_verified, supported) gives ('OFF-DOMAIN', true, false) 38, ('SUPPORTED', true, true) 5, ('UNBACKED', None/absent, false) 16, ('UNBACKED', true, false) 6. So {counter_evidence_verified absent} = 16 while {primary_defect_class = UNBACKED AND supported = false} = 22: the absent set is a PROPER SUBSET, and the sentence also contradicted its own cell (which correctly reports UNBACKED 22). THE CORRECT STATEMENT, which is the correction of record: all 16 absent-verified rows are UNBACKED with supported=false, reason_code 'evidence_absent' and empty cited_evidence, at counter_uncertainty 0.95-1.0 (per bundle de 1 / fr 4 / it 11, the same partition the accepted canvas lock amber 1/4/11 measures); UNBACKED totals 22, and the other 6 carry counter_evidence_verified=true with 52-287 cited quotes and fail for CONTENT reasons instead (reason_code 'no_domain_anchor' 2, 'no_intent_marker' 4; counter_uncertainty 0.25-0.65). WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: the 16 are the evidence-plumbing class the accepted render fix addressed; the 6 are evidence-present-but-insufficient and need classifier work. Collapsing them implies every UNBACKED row is a missing-evidence row and hides the distinction on which product's rebuild-or-decline decision turns. STANDING RULE: before writing 'exactly', 'identical to' or 'all of the' between two counted sets of accepted rows, compute the intersection and both differences, never the two counts; a matching sub-count inside a larger count proves containment at best, never identity; and state WHICH field defines each set (bundle, row language, decision id) because per-bundle and per-row language partitions of the same 16 rows differ. PROVENANCE AND SUPERSESSION: RUN_38906250297.md is claim-bearing history and is NOT edited by the director (never overwrite a claim-bearing output; this repair round's declared scope is state/** plus its own report), so that clause is SUPERSEDED as of director run 38915705490 and is NOT claimable. The correction of record is this entry plus reports/director/RUN_38915705490.md sections 2-3, which govern wherever the two reports differ.

THE SERVED PACKET IS UNDER A STANDING ACCEPTED STOP ORDER; ready_for_owner_session=true IS NOT A CLAIM THE PRODUCT MAY MAKE WHILE EITHER FROZEN BAR IS UNMET. RECOMPUTED THIS RUN from the accepted measurement artifact LABEL_HALF.json, re-fetched from cycle/frontier/frontier-served-packet-falsification/38877700234/team: 65 scored rows = 25 de + 15 fr + 25 it; 5 supported (0.076923) against the frozen ABSOLUTE bar of 1.0; defect classes OFF-DOMAIN 38, UNBACKED 22, SUPPORTED 5, INVERTED 0. The 22 UNBACKED partition EXACTLY (both differences empty, verified by recomputation, not by matching counts) into 16 rows with counter_evidence_verified absent, reason_code evidence_absent, empty cited_evidence, counter_uncertainty 0.95-1.0, and 6 rows with counter_evidence_verified true carrying 52-287 cited quotes that fail on CONTENT (no_intent_marker 4, no_domain_anchor 2, counter_uncertainty 0.25-0.65). OPERATIVE RULE for every lane, team and report: a packet, owner card, disclosure or status field that carries ready_for_owner_session=true, human_gate_ready=true or 'the next step is the owner session' while either accepted bar is unmet is misstating accepted evidence. Product must consume the two bar verdicts as a machine gate input of packet admission. The owner's attention is the scarcest resource in this factory and must not be spent on a packet an independent audit says must not be served. SUPERSESSION CONDITION (v51, precise): this order covers results/product/gate_packet/38839347028 and every artifact describing that packet. It is superseded ONLY by (a) an independent audit gate=PASS of a REBUILT packet whose own artifacts show the frozen rubrics applied as written to the rebuilt bytes (labels) and the rebuilt geometry (with the size-based mega-cluster disclosure firing where the share >= 0.5), with a serve recommendation that explicitly replaces the DO-NOT-SERVE verdict; or (b) an accepted bounded negative converting the map-versus-ranked-list choice into ONE explicit owner product decision. Neither Product nor the Director may declare the order lifted by narrative, by a component promotion, or by the classifier's 1.0 support-among-emitted number taken in isolation.
